label: Bible Study
prompt: For we are strangers before thee, and sojourners, as were all our fathers: our days on the earth are as a _____, and there is none abiding.
verse: For we are strangers before thee, and sojourners, as were all our fathers: our days on the earth are as a shadow, and there is none abiding.
note: David, near the end of his reign, admits that kings are just passing through too.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Now the God of _____, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
verse: Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
note: A benediction for the ages: the God of peace brought again from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep.

label: Sunday School
prompt: That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, _____, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up:
verse: That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up:
note: The royal band's roster appears four times in Daniel 3, sackbut and all — the cue for everyone to bow to the image.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to _____.
verse: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
note: Jesus' mission statement on the Mount: he came to fill the Law and the Prophets full, not to tear them down.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: A good name is better than _____ ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
verse: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
note: A good name beats 'precious ointment' — and in Hebrew the two words even sound alike: shem and shemen.
